title: Safe Autonomous AI Systems: Lessons from Process Control
summary: Riccardo Pirruccio applies fab process-control ideas to governing autonomous AI agents.
learn: His thesis: intelligence and authority scale inversely. A safety logic controller is the dumbest thing in a fab yet has absolute veto power, while advanced process control can only recommend.
His proposed agent design uses Kubernetes and Argo CD as the controller for safety-critical decisions, OpenClaw as the agent runtime, and an observability stack to collect traces.
OpenShell, an ephemeral execution runtime, lets scripts use secrets while the agent has zero exposure to them; he forked it to try to make it work.
Treat it as identity delegation, not separation: an agent's identity must tie back to yours so its access can be scoped. Trust tiers with metrics let the controller graduate trust over time.
He emphasizes fallbacks for reliability and safety, and says he has not gotten the system running yet because Claude kept using SSH to modify the cluster instead of updating the manifest.
